messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered - kvcache (hosted-runtime) OOMs observed in gpu-pool-2 starting 03:04 UTC. Error: kvmap exceeded memory budget; continuous-batching inflight spikes. Alert group: kvcache-ooms.

sam_oncall: I'm taking this. seeing 5xx spike and GC churn. any customer reports yet?

chris_sre: Confirmed OOMs on 3 pods (gpu-pool-2-[1,2,3]). Logs show steady growth in kvmap keys per session. Suspect sticky keys from recent batching change (batch_merge=false -> true) deployed last night.

maria_prodeng: Notified support. Early signals from two hosted customers with longform doc summarization heavy prompts. Latency -> 10-15x for those sessions. No broad SLA breach yet but degraded.

lee_support: Customers A and C reported timeouts ~03:06 UTC. We're triaging comms but waiting for root cause.

ana_ops: (typo: ana_ops) Reproduced locally with long prompt ~120k tokens: continuous batching created one huge prefetched KV entry per session. Dump snippet: ```kvcache.size=243MB session_id=abc123 sticky_keys=18432```

sam_oncall: Ok immediate mitigations: 1) scale down batch window to 50ms 2) enable eviction-by-age for kvmap 3) apply session-prefetch cap 4) pin rollback of batch_merge flag to previous rev. Who can patch the config?

chris_sre: I'm on rollback. Reverting batch_merge flag on serving-config to 2026-03-15 commit id c3f9a2. Patch incoming: ```kubectl set env deploy/kvcache-serving BATCH_MERGE=false -n hosted-runtime && kubectl rollout restart deploy/kvcache-serving -n hosted-runtime```

maria_prodeng: I'll coordinate support msgs. Recommend temporary notice: "We are mitigating elevated latency for some long prompt workloads; engineers are rolling a config change."

lee_support: Acknowledged. I'll queue messaging for affected orgs and add a note to status.redwood.com if we see >2% of accounts impacted.

chris_sre: Rollout done to gpu-pool-2. Monitoring memory trend. Initial tail drop in kvmap keys after restart.

ana_ops: Also pushed an emergency eviction tweak: ```redis-cli -h kvmeta01 eval "return redis.call('EVAL', ... )"``` (abbrev) — basically enforcing max_entries_per_session=4096.

sam_oncall: Good. Can we add a short-term quota: reject requests with >200k prompt bytes for hosted runtime? Want to avoid recurrence while we dig in.

chris_sre: Implemented request_size cap at edge (nginx) for hosted API: ```limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=reqcap:10m rate=10r/s; if ($request_body_bytes > 200000) { return 413; }``` Will push to canary now.

maria_prodeng: Support will offer remediation playbook to customers: reduce prompt size, split sessions, or wait for fully patched rollout.

lee_support: Customer A accepted mitigations; they reduced batch inputs and saw timeouts clear around 03:20 UTC.

sam_oncall: Monitoring graphs: memory per pod trending down, OOMs stopped after config revert + evict cap. Still watching for reappearance.

chris_sre: Next steps: - postmortem, include timeline and root cause (batch_merge interaction with continuous batching + sticky key algorithm) - add automated alert for kvmap growth rate > 10MB/min - add unit/regression tests for long prompt flows - consider limiting default batch merge window for hosted.

maria_prodeng: I'll schedule a follow-up incident review with SRE/Product/Support tomorrow 11:00 UTC. Ops to prepare metrics and a small repro.

sam_oncall: Handoff to chris for next 2 hours of watch. I'm clear. If anything spikes, ping @chris_sre and escalate to oncall-rotation.

chris_sre: Taking handoff. Will also open a blocking PR to add a prefetch cap and a new eviction policy (LRU with age bias).

lee_support: Noted. Closing customer comms loop after final memory stabilization.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged closed for pager. Postmortem ticket: PM-1234 created.

chris_sre: Quick note for postmortem: root cause appears to be a regression in batch-merge logic that caused KV keys to be retained across micro-batches for very long contexts; combined with continuous batching, this amplified KV retention. Action owners assigned in PM-1234.

sam_oncall: Thanks team. Good catch on rollback and caps. I'll add a short blameless summary in the ticket."
